issues.label: Statutory elements of ORS 609.035
issues.why: Court must identify each element the state must prove for maintaining a dangerous dog under the version in effect at trial.

issues.label: Correct version of statute applied
issues.why: Post-conviction amendment means court must ensure it applied the pre-amendment text governing the parties.

issues.label: Mental state / criminal negligence required
issues.why: Court must determine whether and how ORS 161.085(10) criminal negligence applies to the offense and was proven.

issues.label: Proof beyond reasonable doubt on each element
issues.why: Every disputed element must be established to the criminal standard.

issues.label: Provocation by Baby Girl
issues.why: A statutory element—whether injury occurred 'without provocation'—turns on whether Baby Girl bit or nipped Zorro.

issues.label: Whether Zorro's involvement constitutes provocation
issues.why: Court must decide if aggression toward defendant's other dog legally qualifies as provocation of Moki and Gyptian.

issues.label: Location: lawful right to exclude others
issues.why: Element requires the injury to occur where defendant cannot lawfully exclude others, e.g., the public path.

issues.label: Where incident 'began' vs occurred
issues.why: Court treated the beginning location as controlling; correctness of that legal framing must be assessed.

issues.label: Causation of physical injury
issues.why: State must prove defendant's dogs caused the injury to a domestic animal.

issues.label: Baby Girl as 'domestic animal'
issues.why: Statute requires injury to a domestic animal, a definitional element.

issues.label: Defendant as keeper/owner of dogs
issues.why: Liability requires defendant maintain or keep the dogs, though court found it undisputed.

issues.label: Admissibility/use of prior conviction
issues.why: Prior nuisance conviction may be an element or propensity evidence with limits under evidence rules.

issues.label: Whether prior conviction is required element
issues.why: Court must determine if a prior adjudication is a statutory predicate for the dangerous-dog charge.

issues.label: Credibility determinations
issues.why: Court had to weigh conflicting eyewitness accounts (Gaul, Shoesmith vs McCrery).

issues.label: Weight of physical/photographic evidence
issues.why: Fence and knocked-over decorative fence photos bear on competing factual theories.

issues.label: Two separate counts—unit of prosecution
issues.why: Court must justify convicting on two counts (two dogs) from a single incident.

issues.label: Validity of jury waiver
issues.why: Court must ensure defendant knowingly, voluntarily waived jury trial.

issues.label: Pro se defendant safeguards
issues.why: Court must confirm valid waiver of counsel and adequate protection of pro se defendant's rights.

issues.label: Self-defense/defense of animal by dogs
issues.why: Defendant's theory that dogs acted to 'save Zorro' may raise a justification-type defense.

issues.label: Whether trespass by victim affects liability
issues.why: If Baby Girl entered defendant's property, it may bear on the exclusion element or provocation.
